================================================================================
OPERA Sync - Deployment Instructions for Windows Server
================================================================================

DEPLOYMENT PACKAGE CONTENTS:
  - opera-sync-db.exe  (Main executable - no Node.js installation needed!)
  - .env.example       (Configuration template)

================================================================================
STEP 1: Copy Files to OPERA Server
================================================================================

1. Copy these files to the OPERA server at:
   D:\opera-sync\

2. Your directory structure should be:
   D:\opera-sync\
   |-- opera-sync-db.exe
   +-- .env

================================================================================
STEP 2: Configure .env File
================================================================================

1. Rename .env.example to .env

2. Verify these settings in .env:

   # Salesforce credentials
   SF_INSTANCE_URL=https://YOUR_INSTANCE.my.salesforce.com
   SF_CLIENT_ID=<your client id>
   SF_CLIENT_SECRET=<your client secret>
   SF_REFRESH_TOKEN=<your refresh token>

   # OPERA Oracle database
   ORACLE_HOST=<oracle host>
   ORACLE_PORT=1521
   ORACLE_SID=OPERA
   ORACLE_USER=<oracle user>
   ORACLE_PASSWORD=<oracle password>

   # Email notifications
   SMTP_USER=<your gmail address>
   GMAIL_CLIENT_ID=<your gmail client id>
   GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET=<your gmail client secret>
   GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN=<your gmail refresh token>
   EMAIL_TO=<recipient1>,<recipient2>

================================================================================
STEP 3: Test the Application
================================================================================

1. Open PowerShell or Command Prompt
2. Navigate to: cd D:\opera-sync
3. Run: .\opera-sync-db.exe

The application will:
  - Test the Salesforce connection
  - Connect to the OPERA Oracle database
  - Run an initial catch-up sync, then poll for changes on a schedule
  - Send email/Slack alerts on errors (after 3 consecutive failures)

Press Ctrl+C to stop.

================================================================================
STEP 4: Set Up as Windows Service (Optional but Recommended)
================================================================================

To run automatically in the background (see WINDOWS_SERVICE.md for full detail):

1. Download NSSM (Non-Sucking Service Manager): https://nssm.cc/download
2. Extract nssm.exe to D:\opera-sync\
3. Open PowerShell as Administrator
4. Install and configure the service:
   D:\opera-sync\nssm.exe install OPERASync "D:\opera-sync\opera-sync-db.exe"
   D:\opera-sync\nssm.exe set OPERASync AppDirectory "D:\opera-sync"
   D:\opera-sync\nssm.exe set OPERASync Start SERVICE_AUTO_START
5. Start the service:  nssm start OPERASync
6. Check status:       nssm status OPERASync

================================================================================
IMPORTANT NOTES
================================================================================

What it does:
  - Polls the OPERA Oracle database for guests with email/reservation changes
  - Phase 1: looks up the Contact by Email__c and creates it if missing
  - Phase 2: upserts TVRS_Guest__c (with diffing to skip no-op updates)
  - Surfaces guests still missing an email in the front desk report
  - Populates the checkout-survey and check-in Google Sheets
  - Sends email/Slack alerts on errors (after 3 consecutive failures)

What gets synced:
  - Email (used as the unique identifier / external ID)
  - First Name, Last Name
  - City, State, Country
  - Phone (Telephone__c) and Language (Language__c) from Oracle
  - Check-in Date, Check-out Date
  - All required boolean fields (set to false)

Logging:
  - Console output shows real-time activity
  - Logs saved to: D:\opera-sync\logs\opera-sync.log
  - Error logs: D:\opera-sync\logs\opera-sync-errors.log
  - Log rotation: 10MB max, 5 files kept

Andon cord (kill switch):
  - Set ANDON_CORD=true in .env and restart to pause ALL Salesforce writes
    without stopping the service. Useful if SF credentials break: Oracle
    polling, front desk reports, and Sheets sync keep running, and the backlog
    replays to Salesforce once you unset ANDON_CORD and restart.

Security:
  - Keep the .env file secure (contains OAuth tokens and DB credentials)
  - Set file permissions: Right-click .env -> Properties -> Security
  - Only SYSTEM and Administrators should have access

================================================================================
TROUBLESHOOTING
================================================================================

Problem: "Cannot connect to Salesforce"
Solution: Check SF_REFRESH_TOKEN hasn't expired. Re-run the OAuth flow if
          needed. To keep the rest running meanwhile, set ANDON_CORD=true.

Problem: "Email notifications not working"
Solution: Check GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN. Test with: node tests/test-notifications.js

Problem: "No records syncing"
Solution:
  - Verify the ORACLE_* credentials and that the account can read OPERA.* tables
  - Check logs in D:\opera-sync\logs\

Problem: Service won't start
Solution:
  - Check Windows Event Viewer for errors
  - Verify the .env file exists in the same directory as the .exe
  - Run manually first to test: .\opera-sync-db.exe
